Spoiler:
Content Rating
I wanted to put this up top and obvious, to be safe. This game includes some of the following content, none of which are considered 'R' but may be sensitive topics to some individuals:
Video game fantasy violence
Suggestive content (implied text, no graphics)
Alcohol use
There's 1-2 counts of mild language in the whole game. Emphasis on mild; it's a word with an actual English meaning beyond the curse, but I wanted to mention it.
Spoiler:
Synopsis
For over 500 years the country of Lenma has known relative peace as a result of the truce with their Origin Mages.
Masters of their elements, Origin Mages are responsible for keeping their monsters away from human populations. In this, the country maintains stability.
But no system is perfect. Now the repercussions of a tragic event years ago are here as one individual begins a final and bloody quest for justice.
Origin Hunt
is a story-rich game where choices made have lasting impact. The plot is driven forward by realistic and relatable characters, all with their own unique personalities and voices. A challenging turn-based combat system that offers players an absurd amount of control over their team build; play how YOU want to.
Meet the characters you'll get to play as!
Spoiler:
Party Members
Name: Vincent
Class: Half-Bred
Innate Passive:
DarkBlood: Any targets that have Fallen to Vincent are unable to be revived. Additionally, Vincent's recovery rates are increased by 35%
Skill Spoiler:
Transform: Utilize that monster blood and transform! This skill is instant-use in combat.
Name: Mara
Class: Elemental Mage
Skill Spoiler:
Analyze: Reveal enemy elemental weaknesses, along with a description of all their skills! Never be caught off guard in a fight with this instant-use skill.
Skill Spoiler:
Infusion: Infuse Mara with any element, increasing her damage output and resistance of that element by 50%. Great for both offensive and defensive situations.
Name: Ella
Class: Rogue
Innate Passive:
Cunning: Each stack of Cunning increases Ella's damage dealt by 3%, up to 15 stacks. Gain 2 stacks whenever landing a Critical Hit, and 1 stack when gaining or refreshing Beneficial Statuses.
Skill Spoiler:
Moon Hunter: This attack targets all enemies to deal damage according to Ella's massive Agility stat. It also ignores defense when used at night!
Name: Hanson - but don't call him that! He'll only answer in a non-violent way to Squall!
Class: Combat Mage
Innate Passive:
Transgression: Every other turn in combat, Squall gains a Shield. The shield amount gained is based on if he has taken damage that turn or not: if he has, the shield is equal to 16% of his Max Health. If he hasn't taken damage that turn, the shield is equal to 30% of his current Health.
Skill Spoiler:
Alter Time - Accelerate: Increase the party's Agility, reduce their skill cooldowns by 3, and reduce the duration of Immobile statuses by 2 turns. Provides a small heal according to the caster's Magic.
Spoiler:
Game Features
In a self-ranked list of 'good' to 'most exciting!'
Turn-based combat with animated enemies and lively action sequences! The battle screen is never still, from party members using unique skills to enemies crushing said party members with AI designed to create a dynamic challenge.
Achievements, for the completionist inside all of us.
Day/Night Cycle with in-game effects! From skill bonuses to events to the poor guy wearing sunglasses at night.
Gear customization. Can't get enough of ridiculous, complex, over-the-top equipment names?
You'll find plenty of that with  gear traits through the use of equippable augments. turn an enemy's strength against them with damage-reflecting armour! Attack twice with a Violent weapon!
Creating crazy weapons not enough? How about crazy armour with customizable stats, traits, and unique set effect bonuses?
Character Combat Customization: No character is locked into a role. Build your team how you want.  All of this without classes; strategic use of skills and equipment give team-building freedom.
Choices that matter. Choose how to act to your team, and to the general populations. How you interact with others can change how they act towards you!

Spoiler:
Ver. 1.1
Previous version save files are - to my knowledge - compatible. Simply copy the contents of the 'save' folder from the old version to the new version. If there is any issue with loading older save files, I can provide save files at roughly the same point in the game.
System Changes
Animation Optimization. Anyone who experienced lag upon a battle animation playing for the first time in that battle should now have significantly less to no lag!
Drastically reduced enemy respawn timers – farm away! Enemies still remain frozen and passable after fleeing battle for the same amount of time
Preloaded battle HUD items – hopefully no more issues with numbers not showing, or gauges being out of place
Added save reminders at the beginning. Once the whole team is made, these become fewer and farther between
Added some mini side quests from various NPC
Fixed some tile passable errors – such as being able to walk up a cliff ledge by stepping on a flower/grass tile at the cliff’s edge
Minor text changes
Fixed some typos and grammar issues
Improved skill description of ‘Hype Up’ so it’s clear the bonus turn does not apply to allies who already acted
Expanded food item text descriptions – their heal and buff/debuff effects are now listed
Colour-coded more item text descriptions
Balancing
Mara now starts with slightly better armour, and her starting weapon has been buffed slightly
Nerfed Baby Ice Ifrit battle – enemies now have a lower level, lower health, and lower defenses
Skill Buffs: Steal/Mug/Rush skill line: Now ignores defense, and upgrades to have Confuse chances added
Graphical Changes
Totally revamped title screen! Ooh, animated!

posts.author: Cythera
RCXGaming
posts.body:
@Cythera
I took time out of my schedule and played up to an hour and forty minutes, which is wild because that alone is the same length as my own demo.
As for whether I'll play the whole eight hours... it really depends, but I'm leaning on no. Not because I don't like it - in fact, you got some good stuff here. More that I'm overloaded with other things to do.
Pros
:
Spoiler
+
Nice title screen music and effects. Like hot damn these are some cool animations.
+
I like the snappy way the game starts, you're instantly in the shoes of a dude who pissed off some monsters and they push him off a cliff? I'm surprised he doesn't die but I guess that's the classic curse of "player falls off an infinite height and survives" in play
+
Pretty mapping and nice music. Is it custom?
+
Cool pause menu
+
Nice lantern and weather effects
+
Enemies being unable to revive is a cool idea
+
I enjoy the idea of the archives. Any kind of lore book is good to have.
+
Item rarity system? Cool. I tend to like that in games.
+
Ooooh I really like the concept of achievements actually having rewards instead of just being bragging rights. Helps incentivize the player to do them.
+
Augment system for your weapons is pretty cool.
+
You can see enemies on the overworld!! Very nice, especially with how they can respawn after a while. Not only that, I vastly prefer games that have health bars for enemies.
+
I like the animated enemies, I saw this kind of thing in another game and thought it was neat.
+
Vincent's monster form is sick, even if I don't know what the hell he's supposed to be. Is it a custom sprite?
+
Thank god you teleport the player out of the dungeon instead of forcing them to backtrack
+
Interesting lore, but I feel it'd be better spaced apart where it's more relevant. Like during the part after you beat up the Hunter and the Archer, why would Mara decide now is the perfect time to exposition about the Guild if it's still an extremely tense situation where the team is surrounded by angry people?
+
The racism plot is servicable. Not terribly ground-breaking, but as it is it works.
+
The way Celicia shows her power off during her intro cutscene is cool, especially with the icicle towers remaining after she leaves. That, and how she's the one who broke the bridge. It gives a good first impression.
+
You know, it's great that even status effects are counted as resisted and have their own pop ups.
+
I enjoy the combat and the way turns are decided reminds me a lot of the Digimon World DS games, where you can see who has turns coming up soon
+
I like that the characters get their own tutorials when it comes to their skills.
+
The night and day mechanic is pretty cool, although it does get me being all nitpicky wondering if there's more to it beyond cosmetics and giving Ella a straight up buff. (Like why would you want it to be day?)
+
I enjoy the idea that using Scan/Insight doesn't waste Mara's turn. Is this because of Yanfly's Instant Cast?
+
The characters having passive abilities is hella neat.
Cons
:
Spoiler
-
Not sure how well the very industrial title font works with the soothing music if I have to be honest.
-
You have quite a lot of systems in place that could overwhelming for newcomers. I don't like the concept of AP where you have to teach your guys skills instead of getting them on level-up. It adds this unnecessary layer of complexity that feels... strange at the very least. Like I'm not gonna lie, when all these different systems are mashed together in the same game it feels like feature bloat.
-
I don't really like the Soul Trigger system, your stand-in for TP. I feel it would be equally effective as to have all actions boost TP the same way instead of having it be a customizable thing, since it also adds another layer the player has to keep in mind.
-
Why is Dark Fire 3 MP as opposed to the other techs that are 15 and 34 despite the fact it does more or less the same damage as the mid-level Fire spell? The mid-level spells don't do enough to justify using them over the cheaper version. Actually, if Vincent has poor Magic attack then why does he even have magic skills? It seems more intelligent to have him use physical versions of those magic skills.
-
I don't like that the Escape option when you press X during battle isn't shown. It kinda makes it seem like it's not there.
-
It feels very bizarre to just barge into a stranger's house/cabin/whatever and be like "yo can I crash here" like... dude.
-
Wait. They kicked Mara out of her home, forcing her to live in the sticks because she had an affinity for every element? That... seems not-right. You'd think someone with that much potential would be revered as like... the Avatar, or something, and would deserve special attention. If anything I'd rephrase this so she was targeted instead of just vaguely ostracized like her intro cutscene implied.
-
The boss music for the early big fights are a bit too intense and unfitting, even given the situations. The human bosses definitely need something else.
-
The lack of AOE attacks aside from Mara's ultimate feels strange, especially for Monster Vincent. Best example I can think of are the Ice Ifrits that nearly wiped me out due to the lack of AOE. That entire fight felt off because it's four to two, yet you don't have something to make up for it.
-
Grammar: "These are, Mana stones?!"
-
Not shifting the music after Celicia clears out the racists feels offputting, especially when Ella gives us her backstory
-
The regular enemies have too much health for monsters you can fight multiple times. Maybe lower their HP values by quite a bit, since the time used to fight these enemies aren't well utilized if they go on beyond like... three turns at max.
-
"Magic? What does it do?" you've already seen Mara use it hundreds of times before this, Ella. Maybe remove the "magic?" part since the topic is about the special magic Squall can do.
-
I'm not sure how to feel about the dynamic of our main characters. The way Mara treats Vincent like a dog is just weird, even as a joke. I kinda find Ella annoying.
-
6000 HP for the Echo enemy seems very excessive, even as a display fight for Squall's skills. It doesn't help that you immediately face a Gremlin who also has 6000 HP to burn through, making the fights feel very drawn out and HP sponge-y since not much really happens in them.
-
The Kitsune and those little white ghost monsters are way too strong with their AOE MP drain and the fire pillar attack that hits four times. Like jeez, that's excessive.
Bugs:
x
Tileset error - I can't walk to the right here.
x
Uh, what's happening here? Also, is Mara supposed to be in this cutscene? Cause she isn't.
x
Also, she got stuck on the fence after this.
Observations
:
Spoiler
=
If you're gonna have "Person Joined The Party" messages, make sure the text stays on screen for as long as the ME plays, even if it involves waiting.
=
Celicia is your avatar, I see
=
You should take the time to add custom sound effects, as that tends to make your game stand out from other RPG Maker games.
=
What are these little lines on the ground in the plains supposed to be?

posts.author: Cythera
posts.body:
Oh wow, thanks for all the feedback,
@RCXDan
!
Don't worry if you can't finish the demo; I fully understand if you're busy.
Spoiler:
Pros
Thanks! I made the title screen myself, using Gimp, an online text generator, and some of the in-game animations. I am not an artist, so having my title screen liked is big
I really enjoyed the way you summed up the intro, that makes me laugh. Yes, he survives the fall - Vincent falls in water and the currents push him ashore. Yes, it's pushing the 'player falls off a height a survives'. I'm hoping you can forgive me for that cliché
The mapping and music are a mix of RTP and resources I found online - all names are in the credits. The only resources I've bought were the FSM sets and some animations. Thank you, Christmas Steam gift card!
Ah, the load/save screen - you are enjoying another of my lovely artworks! It's a Mog plugin, and it is fun to use
Skipping ahead to the anti-revive passive: This
IS
an awesome idea, I do agree
It's also a big plot point
Vincent's monster form is from ShadowHawkDragon. He (she? pancake?) makes amazing SV sprites! Majority of the animated battlers are theirs, actually. I really recommend checking out their DeviantArt if you are after animated SV battlers
Good point on Mara's expo on the guild; I'll look into that
That's a lot more to the plot that becomes evident over a bit more time, but I shall take it as a compliment that you are enjoying the intro part
Wonderful, I'm glad my antagonist makes such a good first impression
The status effect popup is a modification of a plugin; it was worth the pain and hassle. I get tired of trying to inflict status effects that never land, only to later find out an enemy is immune to them. A resist popup helps
The battle system is Olivia's OTB; she makes high-quality plugins. 100% recommend her stuff
The day/night cycle does have impact outside of combat! Some NPC's change their dialogue (mostly for fun) and some events are only available at certain times. Also, Ella does eventually get a nice 'day' skill that deals double damage in the day on a 3-hit skill. At the start, though, she's a rogue, so she does prefer the dark
Yup, Instant Cast. Lots of character's use this, and some armour effects and items. Helps with balancing, and player convenience in the case of Insight skill
Spoiler:
Cons
I tried a more 'fantasy' font, and it was super hard to read. Now I've grown attached to this font, so I will likely keep, as a personal preference
I'm trying my best to introduce systems to players one at a time, to prevent overwhelming them. Hence why you can't learn skills right from the get-go, or why crafting isn't introduced until you have all characters. I'll always understand my game better than players, so I'm open to anyone saying a feature is introduced too quickly, or not in-depth enough and I'll go back and see what I can change to make it more coherent
I love customizing characters and changing how they can be used in combat, hence the Soul Trigger system. New Soul Triggers are unlocked over time. I get how this added layer may confuse players at the beginning, so I may start all characters with their ideal Soul Trigger active. That way, if players leave it, they'll at least have an optimal SP gain for that character's usual use
Vincent's Dark Magic is based off a % of his Max MP. He is a physical attacker at the start, as his weapon doesn't offer any magic buffs yet, and his magic stat has the slowest level-up growth. I prefer to play him as magic attacker later in the game, after he gains some unique skills via plot, actually!
Thanks, I'll change that so the Escape option is more visible
Vincent is a monster with little social skills - he sees nothing wrong with walking into a cabin and saying 'I sleep here now'. Maybe I'll have Mara comment on that to make it more obvious
With Mara, mages aren't allowed to practice more than one elemental type of magic; it's considered an insult to the Origin Mages. Mages that can use multiple elements are often targeted by less-than-desirable people. I'll rephrase to make that more clear
Aw dang, you don't like the boss music?! I love it
Hm, true, I had to pause and think 'well of course there's aoe - no, no there isn't...' I'll give Vincent an aoe in his monster form early on
Grammar, thank you
Music, thank you
I'm going to circle back to the HP and comment on the balancing at the end...
Haha, nice catch on Ella's dialogue, thanks
The dynamic at the beginning is intended to be awkward; these four don't know each, all come from very different lives, and have very different intentions. They do warm up to each other over time, and do so at a faster rate if you interact nicely with them. Or you can be a jerk, either is fun
Okay, on balancing. First, I do intend for the game to be difficult - such is my desire in RPG's. However, I do not intend for it to be needlessly punishing. I'll definitely consider what you've said on the balancing side. Early game enemies, before you have the whole team, will likely have their HP nerfed. Gremlin has an AI, so he should have been doing...something? I'll look into that. The white ghosts should be rarer enemies, so I think I'm okay with their damage output, though I'll look into nerfing the MP drain, as it's unlikely Mara and Squall have their more reliable MP-recovery instant skills here. The Kitsune, okay, I'll drop the hit count to 3. They've hurt me a few times as well...
Whoops, whoops, and whoops! I'm going to fix those :3

I also played a bit, let me talk about my point
I can’t give too many opinions on the plot story, because my English is not good, and there are cultural differences, so let’s talk about the system.
advantage:
There are many elements of mutual restraint during battle. It seems that the future battle will be very deep, but if you don’t use skills to analyze the weakness of the monster, it will not be displayed?
I like the upgrade and transformation of equipment
Vincent's transformation ability is cool, I like this setting very much, but as the brother above said, his magic attack is really bad! Please highlight his warrior attributes
Conversational facial expressions are very rich, I like their different facial expressions
The day and night system is great, I hope that because of the different day and night, different things will happen, encounter different NPCs, etc., it will be interesting
The achievement system is also great, allowing players to feel satisfied each time they reach a goal
The database function is also very detailed, which makes players not confused when playing games
Disadvantages:
The cave at the beginning even made me want to uninstall it directly. I don’t know if it will be the same in the future.
It is good to darken the angle of view and increase mystery, but the change of the turned light source is almost dizzy, which will cause players to feel disgusted. It is better if only the visible range becomes smaller.
It’s weird that the attack during combat temporarily disappears the targets except the attacker and the designated target.
Why only show one map follower? It makes me lonely
The accessibility of many tiles is not set, for example, you can't walk on the grass, but the bed can walk on it
The town is very big, but there are not many NPCs, it seems very deserted
The monster refreshes slowly, probably because I fight more!
And there are a lot of skills at the beginning, it is difficult for me to get the thrill of learning new skills
Right now I don’t have much game time, but this game is very good, sorry, because I’m lazy, so there is no picture

posts.author: Cythera
posts.body:
Hi
@41728280
, thanks for the feedback! You're bring up very similar points to other play testers regarding cons haha. I'll be making some adjustments before a public demo release, mostly pertaining to:
Vincent's Magic. I don't plan on changing his actual stats, considering how powerful he gets later, though I will add an indicator of some sorts that he is a physical attacker at the start
The flashlight lighting effect. This will be changed to a simple round lantern effect.
More NPC are on their way!
Now I just want to address a few other points of yours that I don't intend on changing at the moment:
No followers on map. It's because of how I do cutscenes,  personal preference, and that you can hide behind them to avoid encounters. Mostly personal preference :3
Non-targets disappearing in combat is for action sequence and animation purposes. Sometimes I would have skill animations play on non targets that are hiding behind targets and that bothered me. Again, this is mostly a personal preference
Thank you again for your feedback! If you think of/find anything else, just let me know

posts.author: RCXGaming

Glad I could be of assistance. You seemed in dire need of help so I figured "why not?", right.
While I'm personally not a fan of not having followers behind you, I understand why you have to do it. Take it from me as a person who has followers be important aspects in cutscenes: it's a lot of extra work that's probably largely unnecessary.

I just tried it out and here are my thoughts:
- Great job on the mapping!  I got stuck in the dark cloudy marsh (gave up b/c the moving clouds bothered me) but I like how much detail there was and the mini-cutscenes were fun.  I hate it when cutscenes are super long and drawn out but yours seemed balanced and you have a good (and well thought out) storyline.

- Having monsters spot the player was neat. That was much nicer than the bright flash and annoying sound many RPG's have.
- This is trivial but I the book laying on the bed (in first cabin?) was a nice touch.
- I *LOVE* how the player sees what objects he gained...without opening a text window!
- Thank you for including a Master Volume option.
- From watching today's livestream, I know you put a lot of work into character development and stats.  I was impressed by that.
Criticisms (mostly just sensory things that are hard for me but might not bug others):
- The battle BGM seemed much louder than the map music.
- Lines in the message box made reading hard on my eyes
- The Save screen is jarring after looking at a dark screen.

Tenrix Forest Path
.  The exit event to
Tenrix Forest
can be missed.  I unknowingly walked around it (accidently found it when turning around to go back to town).  Maybe move the event down one tile?

This really depends on your team configuration, but the skills you should have include: Ella's Stagger, Squall's Star Shot, Vincent's Tackle, and Mara's Light Strike and her Element Charge soul skill. Vincent's Aerial Slice is nice here too, but not critical.

posts.author: kimo
posts.body:
I have been enjoying this game so much that I am not sure if I want to find the end..... (sigh).
@Cythera
I started writing notes shortly after I started your game (ver. 2.0), since you seem to be so open to critique of your project. These are in no particular order and some were written in response to the postings of other people on this forum.
Spoiler
Fog/clouds in swamp (especially at night) seem excessive and will be a turn off (no buy) for some players with vision issues. Lots of players post negative comments about visual/dexterity challenges in other games, so I think it is worth sharing. Also, as a university administrator, I have always been aware of the “limitations” of some people and I think that is often not recognized by many people. *climbing down off soapbox*
Lockpicking task (following the symbols) will not be possible to accomplish for some players with dexterity issues. Should possibly not be speed related? Could an item/skill be found or acquired which would facilitate opening the lock? I almost just quit the game out of frustration because there was no explanation of how to use that skill for the first time. A timed sequence should always be avoided if possible unless you give people at least 2x the time most testers have needed to complete the task.
I personally like your choice of fonts with the slight serifs and curvature for reading flow.
Other than some spelling misteaks (haha!), your choice of grammar and use of semicolons is an author’s choice and I use them for speech pacing (sort of like the excessive use of parentheses being a choice).
I don’t agree with the “gypsy” comment someone made. In fact, people from the Origin region of the term gypsy even refer to themselves as gypsies. Don’t let the PC people of the world change your style. History cannot be white-washed (oh, crap! Was that racial? No. White wash is a painting technique applied to surfaces.) Everyone is entitled to their opinion (even when they’re wrong … haha).
Some battles take too long (i.e 4 enemies with 3000+ HP) to complete, so I find myself avoiding enemies and probably not leveling up enough.
Character status bars (HP, etc) are very thin in vertical height and don’t stand out. I realize this may be a function of some plugin’s fixed attribute, but larger bars would be better for visually challenged players.
Items acquired drift quickly upward on the screen and cannot be read. Is it possible to pause until “Enter/action” key is pressed? Someone else liked this and I understand. It just takes getting used to watch closely as the scrolling occurs. Maybe a larger and a more Times Roman-like font could be used?
There are many people in this world who have red/green color blindness to some degree. You should consider something like a text description (i.e. rare, unique, etc.) when describing traits of particular augments when crafting rather than expecting people to be able to see the difference between colors.
Putting (thoughts) in parentheses is an excellent choice and better than some other techniques I have seen.
Your use of expression icons made me chuckle many times, especially when the 4 characters had different responses to something said.
The game title doesn’t entice me, but I don’t have an alternative. I think how you write the summary/sales pitch will be the most important part of selling this game in the future.
Your world seems to have a very well defined history and timeline.
Setting augments as reusable is a good feature. It allows for more experimentation.
So many buff/debuff icons used, so there should be a chart that indicates what they mean. I have no idea what some of them mean.
Minimal or no enemy respawning. I have always thought this to be the best approach to leveling up characters. Just wipe out all encounters in each area and your character will be at appropriate levels for baddies like “Cerbie/Cuddles”. Unfortunately, some of the battles get a bit tedious in length so I had a tendency to avoid them when possible not knowing your design intent.
Vincent does not give the idea (graphically) that he resembles a monster in the least. What about any character (NPC’s included) would give them identifiable monster traits? I would think a half-bred character would have some residual trait (if even minor like a half-bred goblin with a bigger nose) that would give away multiple heritages. Although the probociscally-challenged folks in the world might take exception, nothing beats a good “honker” and the resulting possible comments.
I have enjoyed your humor and most recently Ella’s realistic conversation in baby-talk with Cuddles.
So far, your characters have been consistent which implies you have character definitions you work from. Do you use personality theory/temperament type when designing characters?
*in his best arnold voice, "I'll be baaaack"*

posts.author: Cythera
posts.body:
~~I just uploaded Ver. 2.1 of Origin Hunt. It's a minor update that fixes the softlock issues that were brought to my attention here. And yes, some typo and grammar errors...~~
@Dagothe
Nothing in particular; just your overall impressions. Any feedback you give is appreciated
@kimo
Okay, I'm going to try to do this in a spoiler...if it goes wrong, please forgive me. I truly am helpless without my edit bar.
Spoiler:
Response
- *sigh* You're not the first to express distaste in the number of fog clouds. I can, and will, point out you can sleep at any inn to push the time to day and make it easier to navigate, but since it is clearly a common critique, I shall relent. The next update will have lowered cloud volume
- I apologize for not explaining the lock pick mini event thoroughly enough! I wanted to do it the least immersion-breaking version possible, so thought having Ella simply offer that small explanation would be better than a 'textbox tutorial'. I will try to make the event more coherent. Also, the combination does not change; it is NOT random. I can finish the sequence before even a third of the time goes by, so I believe it is at a reasonable amount of time for players, especially considering the sequence does not change. There are more lock pick mini events that are randomized, but they are not required for game progression
- Whether I agree with what has been said regarding the term 'gypsy' is neither here nor there to be honest - I absolutely do not want to step on toes, and I recognize cultural differences exist. Now, if someone were to tell me 'pancake' is offensive in their culture, I would certainly look strangely at that claim haha. But I CAN see the term 'gypsy' being touchy, so it was a 'better safe than sorry' call on my behalf. Removing it doesn't change my game, and it removes the possibility of accidently upsetting anyone.
- What enemies were you battling that seemed to have too high an HP? I find throughout the whole game, most random encounters are doable in 2-3 rounds. Maybe 4 if it spawned a set of powerful enemies with smarter AI than the rest of the enemies in the area. It is possible the curve went up too steeply (I suspect this was the shift from Kaldia to Verity you are referring to, but please, correct me if I'm wrong and I'll check out the enemy stats)
- The thin HP bars is both a plugin feature, and my choice. Could I edit them to be bigger, absolutely, though I do not want to take up too much screen space with them honestly.
- I believe I can make the item text popup stay on screen longer, and also increase the size of if too! I never considered it might be difficult for some to read in time. If you're ever in doubt of what you got, new items in your inventory are marked with a 'new' sticker on top of their icon. I get it's not ideal, so I'll see what I can do about making the text stay longer
- I'm not sure what I can do about the colour issue; you can edit the colour of the textbox itself in the options menu? But the colour system is deeply rooted in my project for identifying tier quality, so I fear I don't have a response for this one
- I'm rather fixed on the game title myself, though I'll keep your opinion in mind. I'm still trying to figure out game marketing myself for when it comes to writing summaries and pitches haha
- Oof, you should see my notebooks...I have 3 full notebooks regarding my game. I wrote out a full history timeline, complete with years, characters, etc. I'm glad my efforts are noticed and appreciated ^-^
- If you are talking about the buffs and debuffs on party members, you can press 'X' then 'Status' in combat, to see all party members and the states they're under. That way you don't have to memorize the icons!
- Enemies do respawn; the respawn timers vary depending on enemy and region. Don't quote me on this, but I'm pretty sure the Verity enemies have a respawn of 5 minutes? Around that range. I can certainly lower that timer though, to allow more levelling
- Ahh, limitations of the character generator, and my refusal to make less-than-adorable party members :3 Vincent does have red eyes, and it's mentioned he has lil fangs, but that's all. I think anything more obvious wouldn't actually make sense story-wise; if he's so obviously non-human, why would he ever be allowed in towns? Right now, if he keeps his head down, he can pass for human
- On writing/story in general, I'm happy you're enjoying both of those thus far!
To answer your question, no, I don't really use any of those personality trait lists or character profile tools. Designing characters just...comes naturally to me. I tend to start with general details that are known right away  - age, gender, name, family. Then I build up history. I tend to inject one or two of my own personality traits into every character I write. Then I combine that with their history and that trait to decide how they have grown and what they ultimately act like now. One thing I do that helps me personally is to imagine that character in an everyday situation, like grocery shopping. How do they act, how do they go about buying food, do they interact with other shoppers, etc. I know all my characters' details and favorite foods and least favorite season, and though I don't make that info known to the player, it certainly helps shape that character's personality.
Seriously, writing characters is something I could make a 6-page essay on and just scrape the beginning haha.
Here's hoping that went into a spoiler
If you are where I think you are in-game, you still have...12 hours of gameplay available? No crushing ending yet, never fear! I hope you continue to enjoy my game. I appreciate your feedback and look forward to anymore you want to offer up!

Spoiler:
Strategy
Recommended level: 30
Recommended equipment: Give Vincent your best equipment; without him, you cannot win this fight. Since Presipa is water and a magical attacker, Gold armour is great here. Big bonus if you can roll Water-Spec on some pieces.
How you fight Presipa will depend on how you built your team, but you should definitely have Ella's Stagger skill. It can buy you turns to heal/prep for the next attack. Water Wave, I'm assuming that's the skill you refer to that wipes you, has a 3 turn cooldown; keep that in mind and predict when it could come. Much like Cerbie's Dark Pulse. As for Presipa's passive, yes, it auto-revives her when she falls, and it bypasses SpiritCrush. If only you had a character who could prevent revives...
Good luck against her!
Oh, and I just saw your previous post's edit, and that's a very funny thing with Cerbie's HP! I have fixed it; it was because the pupper Cerbie was a different enemy that transformed into Cerbie. Except, pupper Cerbie had different HP, so Cerbie's HP was randomized between the two values.

As for your feedback...
The crafting point is a limitation of the plugin. When I first started using it, I didn't have enough coding knowledge to make heavy modifications. Now that I could, the system is so deeply rooted it would require way more effort to change, and would absolutely render save files between versions incompatible - something I am trying my best to avoid

Yah, mining is an alternative to fighting enemies for materials. I don't like games that force you to farm for materials when crafting is not optional for progression. So I offer alternatives. They may not be as engaging as combat, but they are options
Yes, gear does have variance in their stats
That is pointed out in the crafting archives. When you craft equipment, you will see the available range in the stats in the description box ex. Defense: 14-20
Weapons have a base stat, then a 'growth level'. That's the number of levels required for a +1 to the stat. Ex. If a scythe has a growth value of 5, and Vincent is level 50, then it's 50/5 = 10. So it's a bonus +10 to the weapon stat. Again, I put this in the archives so players can read it if they want, but not be forced through 5 minutes of texty info-dump

Okay, so the bottom line of numbers is the 'value' line and the top is the 'quantity' line. A number on the top line means there is X of the bottom number in the top row. Ex. Putting a '1' above the '6' means that there is ONE (quantity) number SIX(value) in the top line. So somewhere in the top line, the number 6 has to exist. Let's randomly put that 6 over the 0. Now the quantity is 6 for the value of 0, so there must be SIX zeroes in the top line.
You could fill in the rest with 0's to get 60000010
But that's not valid, because there is a 1 in the top line, but the quantity of ones (that is, the top row number above the bottom row 1) is 0.
[TABLE]
[TR]
[TD]6[/TD]
[TD]0[/TD]
[TD]0[/TD]
[TD]0[/TD]
[TD]0[/TD]
[TD]0[/TD]
[TD]1[/TD]
[TD]0[/TD]
[/TR]
[TR]
[TD]0[/TD]

[TD]2[/TD]
[TD]3[/TD]
[TD]4[/TD]
[TD]5[/TD]
[TD]6[/TD]
[TD]7[/TD]
[/TR]
[/TABLE]
Doesn't work, since there's a zero above the 1, which means there are 'zero' '1's' in the top row.
The top row is basically showing how many of the number below it are in said top row. Using all 0's wouldn't work either, because then the top row would show 0 zeros, which is obviously not the case.

posts.author: kimo
posts.body:
@Cythera
Monster encounter thoughts:
There are 2 areas I have encountered that had signs posted warning of monsters and I have given serious thought to this after my experience in both of them. Here are my suggestions for the respawning issues I have raised. Please understand I am just trying to help you create an epic game because you are on the path to greatness.
Spoiler
Since Vincent is a Straie and apparently one of the most feared monsters in your world, why don’t monsters smell him and instinctually try to keep their distance from Vincent? Respawning monsters is a frequent complaint of many players (especially when they are not visible), so why not populate the areas with signs warning of monsters with a very large amount of wandering monsters (hey, you were warned!) that do not respawn and cannot be easily avoided because of their sheer numbers? And I would suggest you also change the troops’ attack profile so they do not aggressively run after and attack the party and also reduce the troops’ speed to meandering in these areas. Maybe an achievement could be created that would reward a player for clearing out each “Beware, Monsters” area.
I am offering this suggestion, because I almost stopped playing out of frustration when I could not easily explore the Wildlands area especially when I became lost and ended up in the Eastern Forest. Thankfully, you display an area’s name when changing screens. When my strategy is to shut down a game and restart from a save just so I could explore alternative paths, something may be wrong. I realize this changes your approach as a designer, but I think your game will sell if you keep it challenging but less frustrating to explore. After all, where’s the logic in outdoor monsters that repawn so frequently. Now, bats in a cave are a different matter. Been there, done that, even got a t-shirt for it.

My levels were just above 70, so that probably gave me a bit of an advantage.  Here is my strategy
Spoiler:
Defeating The Watcher
Equipment-Everyone should be wearing as much diamondscale as possible.  The Watcher is weak to vulnerable dark so I had Vincent equiped with a bloodthirsty aether scythe customized with a dark symbol and Hunter's tincture.   He'll definitely need one or two soulful armors as you're going to rely heavily upon his aerial storm.  A few boosters in your inventory might be helpful as well.  Have Vincent spam aerial storm every round if you can.
Mara plays a huge role as well.  She'll also need at least  one soulful armor.  Mara has 2 spells, arcane exposure and magic reign.  If Mara casts arcane exposure prior to Vincent's aerial storm, then Vincent should be doing at least 10K damage each round.  In between, Mara can cast magic reign immediately followed by either piercing shadow (magic) or lunar (soul ice and shadow).  So those would be your 2 offensive players.
Ella has a soul stop heart which may or may not stop that regeneration.  It seems to work sometimes, but that might just be a coincidence.  She can sometimes give a good 1-2 punch with soul stagger followed by skill agile slice.  I almost always start her off with soul shatter weakness though and repeat every few rounds.  Otherwise, she's good for using a booster (replenish Vincent's soul points) or a hyper-all or any other support you might need.
Squall is also supportive.  I start with fallen stars then shining aura, alter times if you can, rinse and repeat.
I would say if you can get the Watcher down to less than 10K, try using Ella's stop heart.  I can't guarantee it will work.  More importantly, if he's down to 12K or less, Ella's arcane exposure immediately followed by Vincent's aerial storm should do the trick.

posts.author: Cythera
posts.body:
@Lady_JJ
Spoiler
-No, Ella's Stop Heart skills do not stop The Watcher's health regen. Regen effects are separate, and the Stop Heart skills effect direct healing or life-drain effects.
-The first passive that shows up when you cast Insight is the Armoured passive, which is stopped by SpiritCrush. And against this boss, I heavily reccomand that haha, otherwise your magical damage is reduced by 40% and your physical by 75%. Makes damage The Watcher really difficult.
@kimo
Spoiler
-Ugh, the issue with the HP/MP/SP numbers disappearing is a common occurrence with Mog's Battle HUD plugin
I put a preloader in the game a while ago that stops the problem most of the time, but it does happen once in a blue moon. It corrects itself if you exit the battle, either by winning or fleeing
-SpiritCrush affects one of The Watcher's passives and not the other. It cancels his Armoured passive, but his Rock Will one bypasses SpiritCrush. Trying to deal damage with Armoured active is extremely difficult, so if you're still fighting him, this should be your first move with Ella
-Magic Reign is very powerful for Mara! It's an instant buff! It does consume more MP, but if you equip her with an Overcharge Charm, which makes her magic deal more damage according to her MP Costs, she consistently hits for 9999 against almost every enemy. Even without Overcharge Charm, the buff is substantial enough to justify the extra MP costs. You can get past the extra cost with her Cycle of Magic skill too ;P
-When you say respawning, are you referring to the enemy respawn rates, or are you crafting gear, checking the traits, then reloading the game is the trait is not beneficial? I'll address both; just let me know which one you're referencing
*Enemy Respawn Rates: According to the times you provided, that's 5 minutes between enemy respawn. To me, that's a good chunk of time, so I might have to defer to Lady and Shadow's opinion on that. 5 minutes is plenty of time to explore that little area, heal, move on, etc. If you are waiting for the time to progress to night for Ella, that's a player choice you're making. You can wait on a different map without enemies, or where enemies are less likely to aggro on you
*Reloading for specific traits: This is a player choice, to be honest, plain and simple. I do not forbid reloading for traits or items from chests. I do not force an auto-save after crafting. You are free to reload for traits or items (I do it sometimes!) but that's a player choice. If you fight an enemy, craft an item, and reload to recraft, then you'll have to fight that enemy again. If this is the point you're referencing, I'm a little confused about what you would have me do about it?
-Shadow already gave me heck for the save issue, don't worry! XD I did it to prevent a softlock, as if you save in the whirlpool but are too low-leveled to defeat The Watcher, you're now stuck. Can't progress, can't go back to level up. The solution is allowing saving once again right after The Watcher battle

I'm happy to hear you enjoyed playing my game,
@kimo
I am working on finishing the rest of it up! Story-wise, there's like...5 hours left? It's all the planned side content that is the killer haha. And all the lovely branching possibilities based on player choices... ._. Oooh boi.
Spoiler
-I am working on making the puzzle explanation more coherent. I'll try throwing it at some of my friends and seeing if they can decipher the instructions haha
-You grabbing paper makes me laugh ^-^ I wanted to not-so-subtly hint at players the upcoming area is an easy-to-get-lost-in area. You can just go straight forward to get to the exit, but then you're leaving a giant worm to attack the town...choices and choices...
-The supply locker is a difficult QTE, and is intended to be so. The supplies inside are certainly nice, but by no means necessary to continue. A worthwhile reward for players who get past the lock, but in no way punishes those unable to open it
-I am trying to do better on grammar and passability issues, so players don't have to pick up my slack :3 I know I will miss some here and there, but I will improve at finding them myself - even if I have to run poor Vincent's head into every object on the map!
-Specifically, the issues with HP bars are caused by Mog plugins and Yanfly's Doodads plugin competing for resources. I preload all resources used in Mog plugins to diminish the frequency of this issue happening, but on doodad-heavy maps, sometimes yanfly's plugin wins that war. It does not surprise me one bit this issue happens more in the desert than anywhere else, as the desert is VERY doodad-heavy (all the sandpools are animated doodads). I'm always on the lookout for more permanent solutions to this issue, but for now, I'm afraid the preloader is going to have to suffice! I have no proof on this one, but the amount of weather particles - the sand - in the desert may also have an impact on the HUD loading in properly. Haven't tested that theory though, so don't quote me on it
@ShadowDragon
Spoiler
The clock numbers are indeed 10 and 5 (2 of x and 1 of y equal 25; and y = x/2. So you can math that into 2.5x = 25 or 5y = 25) Look at the lanterns as if they're a clock; note, not all digits are represented, as there are not 12 lanterns. Turn off the 2 in 10 and 5 positions.

Spoiler:
Under-leveled win

So while I can certainly suggest levels for areas, it becomes a gray zone very quickly. The level suggestions come from a rough guesstimate of what skills/equipment characters could potentially have at that point, and how viable a team config they make up. Of course, player freedom and choice comes into that; I can never assume players will play optimally, nor can I assume they've made the worst choices. If you only level up Mara's fire skills and try to battle Presipa, you're not going to have a good time, so you could be level 40 and still losing that fight. Or, you could have made the most optimal plays the whole game and end up beating Watcher at level 40.
When so much of the combat and team is customizable, creating a guide becomes tricky.
That's my problem to sort out though ^-^ I love a challenge, so I'm excited to start plotting out ideas.

No saving inside Retheam; it becomes way too easy to softlock in there because of how I handle events and counters throughout the battles. Also, it's super easy to exit whenever you like; just spam attack on the next fight and I'm certain the enemy/enemies will help you leave quickly!
By 3 enemies, do you mean Rima, Aris, and Cher? They can be fun. In Hyper Mode, it becomes a 5 vs 4 fight. The strategy is to focus-fire down Aris first because of her auto-heal. Try not to inflict stat decreases like Defense Break or Magic Break, as Rima cures them and puts a buff in their place. Instead, bolster your own stats. Shining Aura from Squall is almost mandatory in this fight, and Divinity is nice too; stops Rima from applying all stat breaks.
The tallies are how I keep track of battles won; you get 10 tallies per battle won

For your shadow dragon, head to Spirel, Verity. If you haven't unlocked that area yet, just keep going South from Retheam. It'll be signposted. If you hit the mines, you're one map too far down. In Spirel, check out the south-most building and talk to the guard blocking the way inside. You can scare him away if you have high enough Brutality. Otherwise, you'll need to flip Difficulty Lock on, which runs a level check (65, I believe?) to move the guard.

Yeah, dealing damage to Septimus can be difficult because of both his passive and his Oblivion Wings skill. The Soulful armour trait is random, so I have to say you have just been unlucky. All the traits have an equal chance of being pulled; I don't weight them. There are 27 traits for armour, so you have a 1/27 chance of getting Soulful as the trait. Combined with the bonus proc rate of that specific armour piece, of course. Soulful isn't a weapon trait, so it can never appear on a weapon. All available traits for both weapons and armours are in the Archives, given early in the game at RoseWind.
I'm going to try and create a safety net for that scene issue, based on what you've told me. If I can recreate it, great, I can figure out the cause. If not, at least the safety net will hopefully catch the issue instead of freezing the game.

posts.author: Cythera
posts.body:
Hi lolshtr,  thanks for your feedback! I'll check out the video when I have some more time, but I'll address your points now
Spoiler
Yeah, if you have a higher hz monitor I recommend using the sync FPS option in the options menu
By sections do you mean the different skill types, like skill vs magic vs soul? If so, the section is intentional so players always know what skill type they're using, and also, keeping every skill in one section results in annoying lists to scroll through
Nope, mouse click does not work; it says on the screen to use the keys to exit the end battle scene
'Immune' doesn't fit the number spreadsheet with the game font and size :3 I'd have to enlarge the whole sheet and change the size of everything
That's, uh, that's odd haha. I haven't changed that skill for a few updates. I'll fix that!
Critical hits only deal 180% compared to the engine default of 300%. If you find yourself dying to critical hits, check your states. A critical hit on a character with defense break or brand will hurt
The boat can only be left on docks; not on shorelines
Yes, the critical buff skills can be upgraded to be instant-use
Gremlin isn't meant to be a hard boss to be honest, just a mini boss to make sure players are paying attention to combat mechanics thus far. If you found Gremlin easy, then it means you're using your team efficiently, so yeah, I reward players for that
For the upgrade skill, I'm going to assume you mean upgrading Mara's elemental skills. You can upgrade them in any order and don't need to fully upgrade one element before moving to another. So you can learn Fire Blast then Light Strike then Flare if you want.  The first tier spells have a higher status effect chance, and you may need to use them later if enemies start increasing your mana costs...hint hint
The tackle-ram-charge skills deal damage based on target current health. The upgrades do not change the damage formula; only reduce the cool down.  The upgrade benefits are listed on the bottom right when you're in the learn skills scene
As for Mana Wrath, yes, it's powerful. Squall has the highest damage output of the whole party if used properly
You can save almost anywhere in the game (excepting a few dungeons). I only had save reminders in the earlier parts of the game; I didn't want players to feel like I was holding their hand for too long
Also, just adding, if you are defeating Lyla in 1 hit... you are way more powerful than intended at that point in the game lol! I'll have to keep that in mind, as chances are, you were also much stronger than intended for the Gremlin fight too.
Thanks again for your feedback; it'll help me find where I need to better explain things to players. I'll check out the video when I have some spare time

Thanks for the video; I'm going to just type out some of my responses/comments as I watch it
Spoiler
the .exe protects both the assets (art, music, plugins) and my own personal work that went into the game. It does make the initial loading of the game a bit longer, sadly, but worth it.
game file size is due to, in particular, animated battlers and music. The overall playtime is over 30 hours, and I like having unique enemies and music for areas, so it adds up in file size!
I did gather most of the assets back in the beginning, so over the updates, the file size hasn't grown much. Final version should be around the same size
Comedy-Reel is primarily end-game, but does have a few scenes throughout the whole game
Okay, that crash. When you downloaded the file, there is a 'www' folder in there containing a 'save' folder. You cannot remove this. Without it, the game crashes when saving, or changing options. It's to do with the encryption. On the itch page, the download instructions clearly state do not remove the www or the save folder. I haven't received any reports from players or my beta testers that the download file didn't contain the www folder (nor do I have this problem downloading onto my own computer or laptop) so I have to assume it was deleted on your end
Oh, you're playing on a higher HZ monitor; the game is so sped up haha! There is a sync monitor FPS option, but, uh...you need the www folder as mentioned above
Save issue is because of missing www folder
For the human battlers, I used the larger SV Hine sprite, and drew all the hair, clothes, weapons, features, etc on top! The battlers change to match equipped weapons, and there's also costumes you can get. I had a lot of fun drawing them haha
The transform is a state effect actually! I apply the state, and all the magic happens in there. Same actor. I change the image, add skills, take away skills, buff and nerf stats, everything I need is controlled in a single state for Vincent's transform
I honestly never thought of controller support. I don't know how popular controllers are with players? I can certainly look into it, but since the game is so far in development, adding something that...intensive? May be awkward
Just jumping ahead a bit, yup, Mara has all 6 elements. They're a big part of combat! And, actually, the overall plot haha
The item text colour is related to it's tier. So gray is just the colour I use for common items,  green for uncommon, blue for rare, etc. If you couldn't use the item in battle, it wouldn't be in your Inventory in battle, don't worry
All the guards increase defenses by 50% and have a bonus effect; Vincent's restores some HP. Mara's restores a small amount of HP and some MP
I have different skill categories, and you can learn more later. Never fear, I'm not going to leave you with a single skill in its own category!
Thanks for playing and doing a little video! I'd love it if you could give my game another shot once you've added the www and save folders back in; that will allow you to change your options and save, and stop the issues you encountered

I planned to continue playing and giving you proper feedback, but then real life struck (and to be honest, afterwards I simply was to sucked up by creating my own game, to play anything else, shame on me x.x).
But years later, I have returned and I see you are in the middle of an overhaul of Origin Hunt. So hopefully this is a good time to finally play and comment on your game
So let's start! Here is how my run went so far, but I will put in another section, where I'll try to compress my feedback, so you don't have to try and find some hints in a wall of text.
Spoiler:
My Playthrough of Origin Hunt
So let's start! Because I love reading dialogue and want to see as much character interaction as possible I turned on both Comedy Reel and Comment Gab. I am curious what to expect from the comedy lines. Also very nice title screen, creating this feeling of slowly moving through the stars
If I remember correctly, last time you were chased by some bats in the beginning instead of the hunters, right? I think it's a good decision to change that, since the hunters are already an important part of the story, while some monsters chasing you into that cave would probably feel more random and less meaningful.
I just won my first battle! Nice custom battlers and really cool that Vincent fights with a Scythe. I wonder if you can actually change that though, since you are able to equip weapons ... or mabye it's just other scythes. You wouldn't go that crazy and animate different custom battlers for any kind of weapon in your game o.o?
Second encounter and I was kinda worried, how to survive the other beasts in there, but then I got saved by the fact that I heal by level up
I am out of the cave now, wearing a stylish floppy hat, to make sure the hunters definitely won't recognize me, if they are still around.
Oh cool, they can draw their wepons on map!
First Party Member acquired! Accidently stole Maras wood (and less accidently all the stuff at her house x.x) ... I wonder if this will have any consequences. Also I would love to be able to interact with some of the things lying around, aside from just taking items. Like short commentaries from our hero on what he sees. Something about Maras taste in books at the bookshelf, about Vincent being hungry at the apples and so on. Just a bit of jibberjabber, that exploring worthwhile even if there are no chests around.
Fighting with a Fan is very stylish. Is it a theme in this game, that the main characters all use cool exotic weapons?
Okaaaay Vincents Monster Form is pretty Badass. Now that I saw it again I remember from last time, but somehow I was not prepared to how big it actually was. I hope I will meet some other Strais (was it Straie?), who also are able to transform like this. This would make for a great Boss Battle.
I found a calendar with holidays, events etc. Since there is a day/night system and a date in the menu screen ... don't tell me these events are actually taking place if you are in the right location at the right time?! That would be the coolest feature ever :0 I need to copy that calendar.
... I couldn't though. The guy owning the house through me out, because it became to late xDD It's these kind of things that make the world feel alive, I loved that!
Okay, first day of travel is over. Drank some Sangria with Mara in the bar and therefore came to late to inn to get a room. We had to stay in the common room through the night. I guess Mara wasn't to happy about that, but she also did not want to take random dudes #3s offer to sleep in his room, because the terms on that were not that favorable xD
Spent the early morning going through my inventory and the archive, since I have to lern a bit about this country I am trapped in and realized I actually
have
a copy of that calendar! But now it's time to start our journey again!
...
Just got eaten by wolfs. I will remember to save regularly from now on x.x
Ooh, I met another Half-Bred, but did not catch if he's the same species as Vincent. However Ella joined the team. We had one condition, though: She must wear the gang uniform's floppy hat!
We did not make a good first impression though. After leraning about her skills, we got killed by an Alpha Varina with her fairy lights. Those are nasty!
Change of perspective for a cut scene. And I thought that mage was nice girl! It's her on your avatar, right? Guess she'll play a bigger role than just being a short middle boss then.
I couldn't find Half-Bred Bro on traveler path. Probably because the floppy hats keep slipping down over our eyes. Will keep them though, no matter what.
The bridge is gone. Expecting the hunters to lay in wait anywhere now.
Hmm, I just got a random crash on my way to Ezras Lake. Luckily I saved just a few minutes ago. Game just froze, no idea why. Maybe it's the known MV Crash bug?
Yaay Team Member #4! I remember him to be a crazy damage dealer with his shields, who just disguises to be the party healer. And because I knew he would appear at some point I bought an extra floppy hat. Also I was right about the hunters, but it were just the baby ones, we already fought. Didn't even need to show my monster form to scare them off. Time to finally hop on that boat!
On now, another freeze, in my first battle on the water. But again, I saved right before, so no progress lost.
Wowow, this Gremlim looks like the first boss battle. Amazing Sprite! Is there lore about your monsters? I want to know more about this guy!
Did you all the pixel work for those animated enemies? I mean, I know a few sources of animated RTP Enemies, but those you use do not look familar.
Made it through the gusty plains, but RoseWind port is
also
closed! Poor Vincent will probably spent the rest of his life running from one town to the other, just a step behind those closing paths. While the team is scattered in the town I will let of some steam by ... saving a cat in the plains. Her I did find at least xD Half-Bred Bro is probably still waiting in the forest of Travelers Past for someone to find him ...
Back into town, Ella talked me into helping her to stroll off and steal some cherries. Who am I to tell her that's wrong after looting all of Maras stuff just a few days ago?
I also tried to find what's wrong with Squalls body odor, but telling him how irritating his smell is did not make him more talkative. Also what does he mean, it benefits him to sent poor little me off to my home? I mean he knows about the brand and all the bad stuff that probably happens because of me and still ... don't know. I have to keep an eye of that guy and his smell and his no, no I am a harmless healer, even though I can crush everything with my glorified stick! Also him wearing a staff ruins my team of unique weapon wielders! (Probably I am just trying to make him sound bad, because he didn't like my jokes. Will go to Mara then. She has the same great taste in puns as I have)
At least he lectured me about the whole crafting thingy and the equipment growss! Does that mean my floppy hats can level up with me?!
Aaaah, I let my guard down for one moment and now someone jumped on my back! I told you they where laying in wait somewhere! Damn it and I can't even change into monster form and eat him up, because the Demo ands here. Haha, after your last post in this thread I somehow expected to get the full 75 hours that you are done with in this one demo. Reading it again, I don't know why I thought that though. Then I gues I'll cut it here and go on to the feedback!
Spoiler:
Feedback
Things I like about Origin Hunt:
The Title Screen!
Nice choice of weapons for our heros!
I love the animated character sprites!
But the ones for Vincents monster for and for the Gremlim I love even more!
Good mixture of battle and dialogue
Did not encounter the special events from the calendar yet, but I have such high hopes for this feature!
Day/night cirlce works out pretty good, with people throwing you out and closing their doors
The world seems rich in lore and history, I hope there is a lot to come in the archive
Interesting skill emchanics for the main characters. I guess that will play a greater role when the enemies also become harder
The heros are also pretty likeable, especially when they do not get along
Choices! I love choices! Super curious to see how they will effect the game
The crafting system seems very extensive, in a good way. Spend a llot of time tinkering after the demo did end, just for fun.
The whole game seemes really plished, I did not encounter any bug worth mentioning
Things you might want to change:
I would love to be able to interact with the surroundings with a bit of dialogue here and there. Just short lines about the books on the shelfs, the little things people have in their houses or decorations in the cities. If the main characters had something to say about the stuff they see, I would be far more interested in exploring, instead of just running from one chest to the next. For players who are less into dialogue you could even mix in some hidden items.
Battles feel a bit to easy to me. I died twice, but only because of my own carelessness, not because it was a real challenge. I found so many potions that I did not once have to buy anything and even the ones I found I did not need most of the time, because of the level up healing.
Maybe you want to thin out the variety of enemies a bit. In general it's a good thing, of course, but there are so many different enemies in such a short time span, that they don't feel different at all to me. I did not need to find out about their weaknesses, because chances were high, that the next encounter would have totally different monsters to fight.
Talking about that, Maras analyse spell did not feal very useful, because more often than not, it did not even reveal the enemies weakness, while the description of their attack did not mean much to me (might change though, when the plot thickens and the game becomes harder)
If you should decide to make the battles harder, autosaves would be a very nice feature! I had to replay a whole section the first time I died (but of course, being smart enough to save is actually something you could expect from your players^^)
Something probably only gamdevs or people who play a lot of rpg maker games will care about: With all the customization you did, it would fit in very nice if you also changed some of the default menu sound effects.
Bugs & other issues
Had this strange game freeze a couple of times, always totally random. If you did not install the fix yet, I would guess it is the known MV Crash thing.
EDIT: Realized I am talking about the
fix
, without linking it, in case you really don't have it.
When leaving the town to the south on the most right tile you appear on the bank:
I feel as if its intentional, that she looks downwar during the cutscene, but it still looks a bit off to me:
You can walk under the boat. Also, it looks a bit weird that the lake is so narrow at this place, when you start of with the boat, maybe you want to widen the gap between the isles a little bit:
Typos:
I am not a native speaker, so I won't catch to much of those. Also no guarantee there is any truth in what I think to know about english garmmar and spelling^^
I think there is a space missing between "hunters, labourers"
Is it "wondered" or would it be "wandered" in this case?
All in All:
I really liked it! I liked it the first time I played it too and I feel super guilty for not coming back to you, even though I said I would x.x I'd be definitely in for the full version. I think your biggest strengths are your characters: Their interactions as well as their battle mechanics. If you had to chose what to perfect on your game, I would concentrate on these things, since there are no obvious "weaknesses" to burn out in my opinion. I mean of course you could spent a lot of time with beautiful parralax mapping or fully custom walking sprites or something, but the things that made me want to continue playing even after the demo was over, where the characters and the battles. So if you still want to work on it, after completing the story, I think throwing in even more character interactions and creating even more engaging battles would have the biggest impact on Origin Hunt, because those are the things that will make people play it and love it

posts.body:
@coucassi
Ugh, sorry for the super delayed reply. I've been down for a week now with a nasty flu.
For some reason the forum isn't letting me quote your last message - or maybe brain too foggy to do it properly, I dunno haha.
Comedy Reel is an option because some of the jokes are 4th wall breaking, and I know some people don't like that in games. I don't always like that in games/movies/books.
I am currently taking a look at the enemy distribution in my game. I do actually like what you said, and find myself agreeing with it: too many enemies in short areas means each enemy is really...unmemorable. Yes, I can say early game areas are meant to be shorter and the mechanics less complex...but it should be enjoyable, and reflect what players can expect for the rest of the game. It's not really fair on the player for me to tone down difficulty or complexity early game, set the false standard, and then dump this huge spike on them to the 'intended' difficulty.
To this effect, I'm dropping an enemy type here and there, improving early game enemy AI and skillsets. Troops are being tweaked a bit too, so I can give more synergy
Autosaves on additional save slots: alright. I admit it. My reason for not adding autosaves is twofold. Yes, I'm not a fan. But also because...my save/load screen graphic is for three slots. And, I don't want to remake the graphics and change the position of stuff to make room for more slots
And I will definitely keep you in mind for testing when the game is done. There's certainly going to be a lot of testing needed before full release >.>
In game-general news, I have had to download a flowchart software to help me out with mapping the final boss's AI...it was getting a bit too complex to just wing in MV.
I don't use planning software. I have notebooks I write bullet-point thoughts into, and a Word document I write my changes into. Needing to actually have a plan is...new to me.
Hey, want to see some fun stats?
Origin Hunt is at a staggering 670 maps, minus about a dozen for organization maps and an event template map
41 unique boss enemies (less than 41 boss
fights
because some of them are in the same battle)
Approx. 500 unique skills
Approx. 300 states and passives
And of course...a way to deal almost 80K of damage! ...
after
enemy defenses.
I have a lot more cool stuff I wanna share. But I'm pretty sure ya'll just want me to hurry up and finish the dang game already! So I guess you'll have to wait to see it all
